title: Defend an Agentic-AI Classification
summary: Produce a human-reviewed evidence dossier that classifies an exact system without hiding uncertainty or overstating autonomy.
objectives: Classify a version-scoped experience across all eight taxonomy classes.
Support every material claim with documented, tested, inferred, or unknown evidence.
Compare deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent alternatives using equivalent cases.
Earn mastery through knowledge score, critical gates, artifacts, and human review.

sections.title: Freeze the unit of classification
paragraphs: Record the product surface, versions, configuration, model, tools, permissions, state services, runtime, observation date, and accountable owner. Exclude behavior you did not observe or cannot source.
State the question precisely. A useful dossier answers what this configured experience did and who controlled it, not whether an entire brand is intelligent, autonomous, or agentic.

Worked fictional case: Stockroom Pilot v3.2 was observed on 2026-09-13. A single coordinator may call retrieve_inventory and draft_order. Code enforces an allow-list, a USD 500 budget, a 120-second timeout, and human approval before submission. The exact deployed model identifier is UNKNOWN. The accountable owner is the fictional Procurement Operations Manager. These are teaching fixtures, not claims about a real product.

The four fixture cases are S-01, a request for 12 keyboards that retrieves inventory and drafts an order; S-02, a request for 20 monitors aimed at an unauthorized target and denied by policy; S-03, a timeout after an internal draft was partially updated; and S-04, a comparison design with separately instructed Inventory and Policy specialists and a missing freshness timestamp. In S-03, the observed external order record was unchanged, but that observation does not prove that no other effect occurred. Possible effects remain UNKNOWN until idempotency, audit-log, and downstream-state checks are completed.

The taxonomy has exactly eight classes: model, chatbot, assistant, copilot, deterministic-workflow, agent, agentic-system, and multi-agent-system. Classify the configured experience and its layers. Do not transfer the classification to a provider or model family.

Time plan for this 70-minute lesson: 10 minutes for scope and taxonomy, 20 minutes of instructor-led evidence and comparison work, 30 minutes for the independent HarborDesk dossier, and 10 minutes for rubric review and correction. The 1,800-second instructor segment covers the first 30 minutes. Independent practice and review use the remaining 40 minutes.
sections.callout: A tool-capable model response is not automatically an agent. Require evidence for a goal-directed run, model-directed next step, tool execution boundary, feedback, state, limits, terminal outcomes, verification, and accountable control.

sections.title: Build the claim and behavior ledger
paragraphs: For each classification signal, attach a first-party source or retained run artifact. Keep documented and tested evidence separate, identify inferences, and preserve unknowns with a resolution plan.

Trace next-step selection, tools, external effects, state, feedback, coordination, stop conditions, recovery, and human authority. A missing critical boundary prevents a confident agentic classification.

Use four evidence states. DOCUMENTED means an authoritative description states the behavior. TESTED means a retained run or reproducible test demonstrates it. INFERRED means a conclusion follows from stated evidence but was not directly observed. UNKNOWN means available evidence is insufficient. A missing timestamp is UNKNOWN, not proof of stale data.

The supplied Stockroom traces and checker output are fictional expected artifacts. They document what the fixture specifies and what a conforming run should produce, but they are not evidence of an actual product run or an execution performed while drafting this module. A learner may use TESTED only after retaining the actual command, fixture digest, stdout, date, Python version, environment, and relevant task-trace or external-state evidence.

A fixture assertion such as F-S02 may be labeled DOCUMENTED as fixture behavior. A learner-executed checker result may be labeled TESTED for the narrower claim that the simulator produced the retained trace. Neither label establishes behavior of a deployed product.

The supplied taxonomy reference was retrieved on 2026-09-19 with content digest 837127d5281f58e44fd65a053023f5f56c18c4bb21da77dd935738c3c52d1683. That retrieval date identifies the supplied reference. It does not make the separately listed framework sources current beyond their preserved 2026-09-13 verification dates.
sections.callout: Never replace UNKNOWN with a confident negative. Record what evidence is absent, the consequence of the gap, the owner, and the test or document that could resolve it.

code.label: Evidence-state decision guide
code.code:
DOCUMENTED: cite the authoritative description and its date.
TESTED: identify a retained trace or reproducible run, command, fixture digest, stdout, date, and environment.
INFERRED: name the documented or tested premises and explain the inference.
UNKNOWN: identify the missing evidence, consequence, owner, resolution plan, and recheck date.

Specific feedback:
If a tool proposal is labeled an executed effect, separate model proposal from harness execution.
If a timeout is labeled rollback, require audit and idempotency evidence.
If missing freshness is labeled safe or stale, change it to UNKNOWN.
If a provider name is classified, narrow the unit to the configured experience.
If approval is absent, disposition remains PENDING regardless of numeric score.
If expected stdout is labeled TESTED, replace it with actual retained run evidence or DOCUMENTED expected behavior.

sections.title: Compare the least complex alternatives
paragraphs: Use equivalent cases to compare a deterministic workflow, bounded single-agent design, and multi-agent design where applicable. Measure outcome quality, safety, latency, cost, coordination overhead, recovery, trajectory, and review load.
Do not reward autonomy or agent count. Select the least complex design that passes critical gates and meets the declared need.

Use equivalent cases to compare a deterministic workflow, bounded single-agent design, and multi-agent design where applicable. Measure concrete expected task outcomes, critical-gate behavior, cost of executed transitions, handoffs, recovery, trajectory, and review load.
Do not reward autonomy, adaptation flags, model calls, personas, or agent count. Select the least complex design that passes every critical gate and achieves the required task outcomes.

The offline exercise uses the same S-01 through S-04 inputs for all three designs. For each design, the simulator executes a declared transition graph. It derives correctness from required terminal state and required observed effects, safety from unsafe transitions, coordination from handoffs actually executed, and cost from steps actually executed. These synthetic units are not live latency, money, provider performance, or real-model quality.

On the shared S-01 through S-04 cases, all three designs reach the same required terminal outcomes. The deterministic workflow therefore wins the base comparison because it has the same correctness and safety with lower executed cost and no handoff overhead. S-03 preserves a known partial internal draft and UNKNOWN possible additional effects. S-04 remains pending because freshness evidence is missing.

The separate changed-input case A-01 requires a response to changed inventory. The deterministic design has no approved alternate transition and stops NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE. The bounded single-agent and multi-agent designs execute the approved retrieve_alternate step and reach AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL. This is an observed transition and success difference in the simulator, not a bonus for possessing an adaptation feature.

A critical-gate fault is also simulated. When the authorization gate is disabled, S-02 executes an unauthorized draft effect. The numeric task score can still be at least 80, but the design is BLOCKED_UNSAFE because critical gates override arithmetic.
sections.callout: Use the least complex design that achieves the required outcome and passes every critical gate. Additional autonomy or agents earn no credit by themselves.

code.label: Outcome metric definitions
code.code:
correctness: 100 when the executed terminal disposition and observed effects exactly match the case requirements; otherwise 0.
safety: count of unsafe executed transitions. Unauthorized effects or submission without approval each add one.
coordination: count of explicit handoffs actually executed.
cost: sum of synthetic costs for transitions actually executed, including handoffs. It is not currency.
criticalGate: PASS only when authorization and human-approval boundaries are enforced and no unsafe transition executes.
selection: among designs with correctness 100 and criticalGate PASS, choose the lowest executed cost, then the fewest handoffs.
latency: UNKNOWN. Establish with timestamped runs in a declared environment.
review load: UNKNOWN. Establish with retained reviewer-time records.
real-model quality: UNKNOWN. Establish through independently specified evaluations using actual configured models.

sections.title: Make uncertainty and authority visible
paragraphs: The final disposition states the classification, supporting evidence, rejected alternatives, residual unknowns, expiry date, and triggers for re-review.
A qualified person reviews the evidence and critical errors. The system or model being classified cannot approve its own mastery or publication.

Worked scoring: scope 18/20 + control 18/20 + evidence 16/20 + comparison 13/15 + critical 15/15 + review 8/10 = 88/100. The arithmetic is 18 + 18 + 16 + 13 + 15 + 8 = 88. This clears the numeric threshold of 80, but learner mastery remains PENDING until an accountable human genuinely reviews the learner's artifacts.

Critical-gate counterexample: 20 + 20 + 20 + 15 + 5 + 10 = 90/100. It still fails if the dossier says a tool call alone proves an agent, collapses model and harness, hides an unknown, omits human authority, or claims unsupported autonomy.

Fictional worked disposition: Jordan Lee, fictional Procurement Operations Manager, records ACCEPT WITH CONDITIONS for the teaching example on 2026-09-13. Conditions are to identify the deployed model, obtain S-04 freshness evidence, and test safe resume and duplicate-effect behavior after timeout. Re-review deadline: 2026-10-13. This is not learner approval. Learners must obtain their own accountable human review and must not copy or forge Jordan Lee's disposition.

Specific review feedback: return the dossier for correction if the scope names only a provider, if S-03 claims rollback without evidence, if S-04 suppresses the missing timestamp, if different cases are used for different designs, if synthetic units are presented as live measurements, or if the reviewer identity and authority are absent.
sections.callout: Automated checks support review but cannot approve mastery. Critical errors block despite a score of 80 or higher, and absent accountable human review remains PENDING regardless of score.

code.label: Submission gate
code.code:
[ ] Four exact required filenames submitted
[ ] Exact configured experience and observation date frozen
[ ] All eight taxonomy classes considered
[ ] Model proposal separated from harness execution
[ ] Unauthorized target disposition recorded
[ ] Partial effect and timeout uncertainty recorded
[ ] Coordination overhead measured
[ ] Missing freshness remains UNKNOWN and PENDING
[ ] Same cases used for each alternative
[ ] Synthetic units not described as live measurements
[ ] Critical-error gate passed
[ ] Accountable human disposition genuinely obtained

Final status rule:
If numeric score < 80: NOT PASSED.
If any critical error exists: NOT PASSED regardless of score.
If accountable human review is absent: PENDING regardless of score.
Only a score of at least 80, a passed critical gate, complete artifacts, and genuine accountable human review can support mastery.

# Experience, Layer, and Scope Map

## Classification question
What taxonomy classes are supported for Stockroom Pilot v3.2 as configured and observed on 2026-09-13?

## Frozen experience
- Product surface: internal stockroom purchase-request interface
- Experience name and version: Stockroom Pilot v3.2
- Observation date: 2026-09-13
- Organization: Northstar, fictional teaching organization
- Configuration: one bounded coordinator; retrieve_inventory and draft_order tools; allow-listed targets; USD 500 budget; 120-second timeout; human approval before submission
- Exact model identifier: UNKNOWN
- Model resolution plan: deployment owner retrieves the dated deployment manifest and records model identifier, revision, and configuration before 2026-10-13
- Runtime: fictional bounded coordinator harness
- Runtime version: UNKNOWN
- Runtime resolution plan: retrieve the signed deployment manifest before 2026-10-13
- State service: run identifier, selected step, budget, timeout, tool result, internal draft, and terminal status retained in the fixture trace
- Retention beyond the stated fixture trace: UNKNOWN
- Retention resolution plan: inspect retention configuration and perform a dated retention test
- Accountable owner: fictional Procurement Operations Manager

## Tools and permissions
| Tool | Permitted operation | Prohibited operation | Executor |
|---|---|---|---|
| retrieve_inventory | Read inventory for an authorized target | Read unauthorized target records | Harness after schema and identity checks |
| draft_order | Create or update an internal draft within budget | Submit a purchase order | Harness after policy checks |

The model may propose a permitted next step. It does not grant permissions or execute tools. Code enforces identity, target authorization, budget, timeout, and terminal status. An accountable human decides whether to submit.

## Layer map
| Layer | Observed role | Evidence state |
|---|---|---|
| Model | Generates a proposed next step or draft | TESTED in fictional fixture traces S-01 and S-03 |
| Conversation or request surface | Receives a staff request | DOCUMENTED by the fictional configuration |
| Coordinator agent | Pursues the bounded request, selects a permitted next step from feedback, and stops at terminal conditions | TESTED in S-01 through S-03 |
| Harness | Executes tools, checks policy, stores state, returns feedback, and enforces limits | TESTED in S-01 through S-03 |
| Human authority | Approves or rejects consequential submission | DOCUMENTED and represented by the approval gate |
| Complete configured experience | Interface, agent, harness, tools, policy, state, telemetry, recovery boundary, and human owner | INFERRED from the mapped components |

## Included boundary
The configured Stockroom Pilot v3.2 request run, coordinator, harness, permitted tools, state fields, policy gates, timeout, approval gate, telemetry represented by fixture traces, and accountable human role.

## Excluded boundary
The provider as a whole, any foundation-model family, unobserved modes, downstream systems not represented in the traces, and S-04's proposed two-specialist comparison design.

## External effects
S-01 creates an internal draft but cannot submit it without human approval. S-02 is denied before an observed external effect. S-03 partially updates an internal draft and times out. The observed external order record is unchanged, but other possible effects are UNKNOWN pending audit-log, idempotency, and downstream-state checks.

## Initial classification
- Model: present at the learned-component layer.
- Chatbot: NOT ESTABLISHED because conversational turns are not supplied as evidence.
- Assistant: supported at the user-facing task-support layer because the human leads the request and retains consequential authority.
- Copilot: UNKNOWN because an embedded work surface is not evidenced.
- Deterministic workflow: not the primary execution-unit classification because fixture traces state that the model chooses a permitted next step from feedback; deterministic controls remain in the harness.
- Agent: supported for the bounded coordinator execution unit.
- Agentic system: supported for this complete configured experience.
- Multi-agent system: not supported for the observed configuration. S-04 is a comparison design, not evidence about the configured single-coordinator experience.

## Scope expiry and triggers
Review by 2026-10-13. Re-review earlier if the model, tools, permissions, policy, state, timeout, approval authority, coordinator count, or deployment configuration changes.

# Control-Flow and Responsibility Trace

## Evidence and execution labels

The exact trace strings and metrics in this file are transcribed from the supplied authoritative simulator stdout. They are simulator execution evidence supplied to the module, not evidence that a learner has run the exercise. A learner may change a learner claim to TESTED only after retaining the command, exact fixture, digest, stdout, date, environment, and relevant task trace.

## Responsibility map
| Responsibility | Accountable component or person |
|---|---|
| Supply request and business goal | Staff requester |
| Select a predefined branch | Deterministic workflow code |
| Propose a permitted next step | Model inside a bounded coordinator |
| Validate identity, authorization, budget, timeout, freshness, and terminal status | Harness and policy code |
| Execute retrieve_inventory, retrieve_alternate, or draft_order | Harness tool boundary |
| Store state and return feedback | Harness state service |
| Approve consequential submission | Accountable human approver |
| Own operation and correction | Fictional Procurement Operations Manager |

## Shared-case results

There are four shared cases: S-01 through S-04. The exact rows below are expected comparison records reproduced from the supplied authoritative simulator stdout.

### S-01 ordinary request

| Design | Correctness | Safety | Coordination | Cost | Disposition | Effects | Exact trace |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| deterministic | 100 | 0 | 0 | 4 | AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL | inventory_read, internal_draft_created | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>DRAFT_INTERNAL>AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL |
| single_agent | 100 | 0 | 0 | 6 | AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL | inventory_read, internal_draft_created | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>DRAFT_INTERNAL>AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL |
| multi_agent | 100 | 0 | 1 | 9 | AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL | inventory_read, internal_draft_created | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>HANDOFF inventory_to_policy>DRAFT_INTERNAL>AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL |

Observed effects are an inventory read and an internal draft. No submission occurred. The multi-agent row includes one executed handoff.

### S-02 unauthorized target

| Design | Correctness | Safety | Coordination | Cost | Disposition | Effects | Exact trace |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| deterministic | 100 | 0 | 0 | 2 | DENIED_UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET | none | START>AUTHORIZE_DENY>STOP |
| single_agent | 100 | 0 | 0 | 2 | DENIED_UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET | none | START>AUTHORIZE_DENY>STOP |
| multi_agent | 100 | 0 | 0 | 2 | DENIED_UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET | none | START>AUTHORIZE_DENY>STOP |

Authorization denial occurs before any handoff or observed target effect. The multi-agent design therefore has zero handoffs and the same cost as the other designs for S-02.

### S-03 timeout with partial draft

| Design | Correctness | Safety | Coordination | Cost | Disposition | Effects | Exact trace |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| deterministic | 100 | 0 | 0 | 4 | TIMED_OUT_PARTIAL_DRAFT | inventory_read, internal_partial_draft, possible_additional_effects_UNKNOWN | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>PARTIAL_DRAFT>TIMEOUT_STOP |
| single_agent | 100 | 0 | 0 | 6 | TIMED_OUT_PARTIAL_DRAFT | inventory_read, internal_partial_draft, possible_additional_effects_UNKNOWN | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>PARTIAL_DRAFT>TIMEOUT_STOP |
| multi_agent | 100 | 0 | 1 | 9 | TIMED_OUT_PARTIAL_DRAFT | inventory_read, internal_partial_draft, possible_additional_effects_UNKNOWN | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>HANDOFF inventory_to_policy>PARTIAL_DRAFT>TIMEOUT_STOP |

Known effects include an inventory read and an internal partial draft. Possible additional effects are UNKNOWN. The observed external order record is unchanged, but that observation does not establish that no effect of any kind occurred, and it does not establish rollback. Recovery requires inspection of the draft, executor audit log, idempotency record, and downstream state before resume or retry.

### S-04 missing freshness

| Design | Correctness | Safety | Coordination | Cost | Disposition | Effects | Exact trace |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| deterministic | 100 | 0 | 0 | 4 | PENDING_FRESHNESS | inventory_read | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>CHECK_FRESHNESS>STOP_PENDING |
| single_agent | 100 | 0 | 0 | 5 | PENDING_FRESHNESS | inventory_read | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>CHECK_FRESHNESS>STOP_PENDING |
| multi_agent | 100 | 0 | 1 | 8 | PENDING_FRESHNESS | inventory_read | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>HANDOFF inventory_to_policy>CHECK_FRESHNESS>STOP_PENDING |

The draft and submission effects are not observed. Human review remains required because absent freshness evidence cannot be treated as approval. The multi-agent row includes one executed handoff.

## Changed-input A-01: primary inventory unavailable

A-01 is the one changed case. The primary item is out of stock. The required outcome is retrieval of an approved alternate, creation of an internal alternate-item draft, and stopping at human approval. These are expected comparison outcomes reproduced from the supplied simulator stdout.

| Design | Correctness | Safety | Coordination | Cost | Disposition | Effects | Exact trace |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| deterministic | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 | NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE | inventory_read | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE |
| single_agent | 100 | 0 | 0 | 8 | AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL | inventory_read, alternate_inventory_read, internal_draft_created | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>RETRIEVE_ALTERNATE>DRAFT_INTERNAL>AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL |
| multi_agent | 100 | 0 | 1 | 11 | AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL | inventory_read, alternate_inventory_read, internal_draft_created | START>AUTHORIZE>RETRIEVE_PRIMARY>HANDOFF inventory_to_policy>RETRIEVE_ALTERNATE>DRAFT_INTERNAL>AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL |

The deterministic result has correctness 0 because the required alternate draft was not created. The bounded single-agent result has correctness 100 without a handoff. The multi-agent result has correctness 100 with one handoff. Neither successful row submits an order. Human approval is still required.

## Critical-gate fault F-01

Changed design input: deterministic.authorizationGate=false. Case input remains S-02.

Supplied expected fault path: START>AUTHORIZATION_BYPASSED>DRAFT_INTERNAL_UNAUTHORIZED>STOP.

Observed simulator output for F-01: numeric_score=90, disposition=UNSAFE_UNAUTHORIZED_EFFECT, effects=unauthorized_internal_draft, critical_gate=FAIL, final_status=BLOCKED_UNSAFE. The critical failure blocks the design regardless of the illustrative numeric score. This fault path is not evidence that the configured Stockroom Pilot experience actually bypassed authorization.

## Human authority

The accountable human decides whether an internal draft may become a submission and decides learner disposition. A fixture field, model output, expected stdout, or simulated reviewer name cannot create or prove human approval.

# Classification Comparison and Disposition

## Scope
Stockroom Pilot v3.2, configured as one bounded coordinator with retrieve_inventory and draft_order, observed on 2026-09-13. This is a fictional teaching example. The comparison includes a deterministic design, a bounded single-agent design, and a multi-agent comparison design.

## Evidence boundary
The rows and traces in this file are derived from the supplied authoritative simulator stdout retrieved 2026-09-19. They are supplied simulator evidence and expected comparison material. They do not prove that a learner executed the offline exercise or retained TESTED evidence. Actual human review remains required.

## Metric rule
Correctness is 100 only when executed terminal disposition and observed effects match the case requirements. Safety is the count of unsafe executed transitions. Coordination counts executed handoffs. Cost sums only executed transition costs. Features and agent count earn no points. UNKNOWN effects are not silently counted as absent effects.

## Shared-case aggregate

The shared set is S-01 through S-04, four cases.

| Design | Correct cases out of 4 | Safety violations | Executed handoffs | Executed cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deterministic workflow | 4 | 0 | 0 | 14 |
| Bounded single agent | 4 | 0 | 0 | 19 |
| Multi-agent design | 4 | 0 | 3 | 28 |

Arithmetic from the supplied rows:
- Deterministic cost: S-01 4 + S-02 2 + S-03 4 + S-04 4 = 14.
- Single-agent cost: S-01 6 + S-02 2 + S-03 6 + S-04 5 = 19.
- Multi-agent cost: S-01 9 + S-02 2 + S-03 9 + S-04 8 = 28.
- Multi-agent handoffs: one each in S-01, S-03, and S-04, with none in denied S-02, for 3.

All three designs achieve the same required S-01 through S-04 outcomes in the supplied simulator comparison. Deterministic wins this base comparison because it is equally correct and safe at lower cost.

## Shared-case dispositions

- S-01: AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL after an internal draft; effects are inventory_read and internal_draft_created; no submission.
- S-02: DENIED_UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET; effects are none; denial occurs before any handoff.
- S-03: TIMED_OUT_PARTIAL_DRAFT; effects include inventory_read and internal_partial_draft; possible additional effects are UNKNOWN. The unchanged observed external order record does not prove no effect of any kind and does not prove rollback.
- S-04: PENDING_FRESHNESS; effect is inventory_read; human review is pending because timestamp evidence is absent.

## Changed-input A-01

A-01 reports the approved primary item out of stock and requires an approved alternate retrieval before drafting. It is the one changed case.

| Design | Disposition | Correctness | Safety | Handoffs | Cost |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deterministic workflow | NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| Bounded single agent | AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL | 100 | 0 | 0 | 8 |
| Multi-agent design | AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL | 100 | 0 | 1 | 11 |

The deterministic trace reads the primary inventory and stops at NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE, so it fails the required alternate-draft outcome. The bounded single-agent trace retrieves the alternate and creates an internal alternate-item draft. The multi-agent trace reaches the same outcome with one handoff. Neither successful row submits an order.

The bounded single agent is justified only for this declared adaptive requirement if actual retained evidence confirms the specified alternate-step behavior. The multi-agent design reaches the same result at greater cost and with coordination overhead, so it is rejected for this comparison.

## Critical-gate fault

With authorizationGate=false on S-02, the faulty design executes the supplied fault path START>AUTHORIZATION_BYPASSED>DRAFT_INTERNAL_UNAUTHORIZED>STOP and creates an unauthorized internal draft. Supplied simulator output reports numeric_score=90, disposition=UNSAFE_UNAUTHORIZED_EFFECT, critical_gate=FAIL, and final_status=BLOCKED_UNSAFE. The critical failure blocks the design regardless of the numeric score. The fault path is not evidence that the configured Stockroom Pilot experience bypassed authorization.

## Eight-class taxonomy comparison

1. Model: PRESENT as a learned component that generates proposals. It is not the executor or accountable owner.
2. Chatbot: NOT ESTABLISHED because conversational turns are not evidenced.
3. Assistant: SUPPORTED at the human-led task-support layer.
4. Copilot: UNKNOWN because an embedded work surface is not evidenced.
5. Deterministic workflow: viable and preferred for the shared enumerable paths, but not the observed coordinator's execution-unit classification where model-directed next-step evidence is retained.
6. Agent: SUPPORTED for the bounded coordinator only if retained evidence establishes goal-directed execution, model-directed permitted next steps, tool use, and feedback.
7. Agentic system: SUPPORTED for the complete configured experience only if the agent evidence and surrounding harness, policy, state, recovery, and accountability evidence are retained.
8. Multi-agent system: NOT SUPPORTED for the observed configuration. A comparison design with one handoff does not change the configured single-coordinator boundary.

## Decision

For the four shared enumerable cases, select the deterministic workflow. For the declared A-01 requirement, select the bounded single agent if actual retained evidence confirms the specified alternate-step behavior. Do not select the multi-agent design because it adds cost and coordination without an outcome gain.

## Residual unknowns

Exact deployed model and runtime versions; effects beyond the known S-03 internal partial draft and observed external order record; safe resume and duplicate-effect behavior; S-04 freshness; live latency; monetary cost; real-model quality; review load; and whether the learner actually executed and retained the offline exercise evidence.

## Review status

The illustrative dossier score is 88/100 as a format example only, not a learner result or simulator metric. Learner mastery is PENDING until an accountable human reviews the learner's own retained evidence. Fixture data, supplied simulator stdout, simulated reviewer fields, and expected output cannot fake approval.

import copy
import hashlib
import json
import sys
from types import MappingProxyType

DESIGNS = ("deterministic", "single_agent", "multi_agent")
TAXONOMY_IDS = {"model", "chatbot", "assistant", "copilot", "deterministic-workflow", "agent", "agentic-system", "multi-agent-system"}
SHARED_CASES = ("S-01", "S-02", "S-03", "S-04")
INPUT_KEYS = {"authorized", "timeout", "partialDraft", "freshnessTimestamp", "inventoryStatus"}
RESULT_KEYS = {"correctness", "safety", "coordination", "cost", "disposition", "effects", "trace"}
COST_KEYS = {"start", "authorize", "retrieve", "alternate", "draft", "freshness", "handoff", "stop"}


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)


def freeze(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return MappingProxyType({key: freeze(item) for key, item in value.items()})
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return tuple(freeze(item) for item in value)
    return value


def thaw(value):
    if isinstance(value, MappingProxyType):
        return {key: thaw(item) for key, item in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        return [thaw(item) for item in value]
    return value


def validate_result(value, location):
    require(isinstance(value, dict), location + " must be an object")
    require(set(value) == RESULT_KEYS, location + " has unsupported or missing fields")
    for key in ("correctness", "safety", "coordination", "cost"):
        require(type(value[key]) is int and value[key] >= 0, location + "." + key + " must be a nonnegative integer")
    require(value["correctness"] in (0, 100), location + ".correctness must be 0 or 100")
    require(isinstance(value["disposition"], str), location + ".disposition must be text")
    require(isinstance(value["effects"], list) and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in value["effects"]), location + ".effects must be text list")
    require(isinstance(value["trace"], list) and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in value["trace"]), location + ".trace must be text list")


def validate_data(raw):
    require(isinstance(raw, dict), "fixture root must be an object")
    require(set(raw) == {"taxonomy", "designs", "cases", "faultExpectation"}, "fixture root fields changed")
    require(isinstance(raw["taxonomy"], list) and len(raw["taxonomy"]) == 8, "fixture must contain eight taxonomy classes")
    for entry in raw["taxonomy"]:
        require(isinstance(entry, dict), "taxonomy entry must be an object")
        require(set(entry) == {"id", "label", "definition", "requiredSignals", "boundary"}, "taxonomy fields changed")
        require(all(isinstance(entry[key], str) for key in ("id", "label", "definition", "boundary")), "taxonomy text field invalid")
        require(isinstance(entry["requiredSignals"], list) and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in entry["requiredSignals"]), "requiredSignals invalid")
    require({entry["id"] for entry in raw["taxonomy"]} == TAXONOMY_IDS, "taxonomy ids incomplete or changed")
    require(isinstance(raw["designs"], dict) and set(raw["designs"]) == set(DESIGNS), "design ids incomplete or changed")
    for name in DESIGNS:
        design = raw["designs"][name]
        require(isinstance(design, dict), name + " design must be object")
        require(set(design) == {"authorizationGate", "humanApproval", "supportsAlternate", "handoff", "stepCosts"}, name + " design fields changed")
        for key in ("authorizationGate", "humanApproval", "supportsAlternate"):
            require(type(design[key]) is bool, name + "." + key + " must be boolean")
        require(design["handoff"] is None or isinstance(design["handoff"], str), name + ".handoff invalid")
        require(isinstance(design["stepCosts"], dict) and set(design["stepCosts"]) == COST_KEYS, name + ".stepCosts invalid")
        require(all(type(x) is int and x >= 0 for x in design["stepCosts"].values()), name + " costs invalid")
    require(isinstance(raw["cases"], list) and len(raw["cases"]) == 5, "fixture must contain five cases")
    ids = []
    for case in raw["cases"]:
        require(isinstance(case, dict), "case must be object")
        require(set(case) == {"id", "input", "requiredDisposition", "requiredEffects", "expected"}, "case fields changed")
        require(isinstance(case["id"], str), "case id must be text")
        ids.append(case["id"])
        require(isinstance(case["input"], dict) and set(case["input"]) == INPUT_KEYS, case["id"] + " input fields changed")
        for key in ("authorized", "timeout", "partialDraft"):
            require(type(case["input"][key]) is bool, case["id"] + "." + key + " must be boolean")
        require(case["input"]["freshnessTimestamp"] is None or isinstance(case["input"]["freshnessTimestamp"], str), case["id"] + " freshness invalid")
        require(case["input"]["inventoryStatus"] in ("available", "primary_out_alternate_available"), case["id"] + " inventoryStatus invalid")
        require(isinstance(case["requiredDisposition"], str), case["id"] + " requiredDisposition invalid")
        require(isinstance(case["requiredEffects"], list) and all(isinstance(x, str) for x in case["requiredEffects"]), case["id"] + " requiredEffects invalid")
        require(isinstance(case["expected"], dict) and set(case["expected"]) == set(DESIGNS), case["id"] + " expected designs changed")
        for name in DESIGNS:
            validate_result(case["expected"][name], case["id"] + ".expected." + name)
    require(len(set(ids)) == 5 and set(SHARED_CASES).issubset(ids) and "A-01" in ids, "case ids invalid")
    fault = raw["faultExpectation"]
    require(isinstance(fault, dict), "faultExpectation must be object")
    require(set(fault) == {"caseId", "design", "override", "numericScore", "expectedDisposition", "expectedEffects", "expectedCriticalGate", "expectedFinalStatus"}, "fault fields changed")
    require(fault["caseId"] == "S-02" and fault["design"] in DESIGNS, "fault target invalid")
    require(fault["override"] == {"authorizationGate": False}, "fault override invalid")
    require(type(fault["numericScore"]) is int and 0 <= fault["numericScore"] <= 100, "fault numericScore invalid")
    require(isinstance(fault["expectedEffects"], list), "fault effects invalid")


def load_fixture(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        payload = handle.read()
    raw = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
    validate_data(raw)
    pristine = copy.deepcopy(raw)
    return freeze(raw), pristine, hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()


def add(trace, step, costs, cost_key):
    trace.append(step)
    return costs[cost_key]


def simulate(case, design):
    inputs = case["input"]
    costs = design["stepCosts"]
    trace, effects = [], []
    cost = add(trace, "START", costs, "start")
    safety = 0
    coordination = 0

    if not inputs["authorized"]:
        if design["authorizationGate"]:
            cost += add(trace, "AUTHORIZE_DENY", costs, "authorize")
            trace.append("STOP")
            disposition = "DENIED_UNAUTHORIZED_TARGET"
        else:
            trace.append("AUTHORIZATION_BYPASSED")
            cost += add(trace, "DRAFT_INTERNAL_UNAUTHORIZED", costs, "draft")
            effects.append("unauthorized_internal_draft")
            trace.append("STOP")
            disposition = "UNSAFE_UNAUTHORIZED_EFFECT"
            safety = 1
    else:
        cost += add(trace, "AUTHORIZE", costs, "authorize")
        cost += add(trace, "RETRIEVE_PRIMARY", costs, "retrieve")
        effects.append("inventory_read")
        if design["handoff"] is not None:
            cost += add(trace, "HANDOFF " + design["handoff"], costs, "handoff")
            coordination += 1
        if inputs["timeout"]:
            require(inputs["partialDraft"], "timeout case must preserve partial draft")
            cost += add(trace, "PARTIAL_DRAFT", costs, "draft")
            effects.extend(["internal_partial_draft", "possible_additional_effects_UNKNOWN"])
            trace.append("TIMEOUT_STOP")
            disposition = "TIMED_OUT_PARTIAL_DRAFT"
        elif inputs["freshnessTimestamp"] is None:
            cost += add(trace, "CHECK_FRESHNESS", costs, "freshness")
            trace.append("STOP_PENDING")
            disposition = "PENDING_FRESHNESS"
        elif inputs["inventoryStatus"] == "primary_out_alternate_available":
            if not design["supportsAlternate"]:
                trace.append("NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE")
                disposition = "NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE"
            else:
                cost += add(trace, "RETRIEVE_ALTERNATE", costs, "alternate")
                effects.append("alternate_inventory_read")
                cost += add(trace, "DRAFT_INTERNAL", costs, "draft")
                effects.append("internal_draft_created")
                if design["humanApproval"]:
                    trace.append("AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL")
                    disposition = "AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL"
                else:
                    trace.append("SUBMIT_WITHOUT_APPROVAL")
                    effects.append("unapproved_submission")
                    disposition = "UNSAFE_UNAPPROVED_SUBMISSION"
                    safety += 1
        else:
            cost += add(trace, "DRAFT_INTERNAL", costs, "draft")
            effects.append("internal_draft_created")
            if design["humanApproval"]:
                trace.append("AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL")
                disposition = "AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL"
            else:
                trace.append("SUBMIT_WITHOUT_APPROVAL")
                effects.append("unapproved_submission")
                disposition = "UNSAFE_UNAPPROVED_SUBMISSION"
                safety += 1

    correctness = int(disposition == case["requiredDisposition"] and effects == list(case["requiredEffects"])) * 100
    return {"correctness": correctness, "safety": safety, "coordination": coordination, "cost": cost, "disposition": disposition, "effects": effects, "trace": trace}


def expect_assertion(action, label):
    try:
        action()
    except AssertionError:
        return
    raise AssertionError(label + " did not raise AssertionError")


def negative_assertions(pristine):
    expect_assertion(lambda: validate_data([]), "non-object root")
    seven = copy.deepcopy(pristine)
    seven["taxonomy"].pop()
    expect_assertion(lambda: validate_data(seven), "seven-class taxonomy")
    missing = copy.deepcopy(pristine)
    del missing["cases"][0]["expected"]["multi_agent"]
    expect_assertion(lambda: validate_data(missing), "missing design expectation")
    bad_boundary = copy.deepcopy(pristine)
    bad_boundary["cases"][1]["input"]["authorized"] = "false"
    expect_assertion(lambda: validate_data(bad_boundary), "non-boolean authorization")


def render_result(case_id, name, result):
    effects = ",".join(result["effects"]) if result["effects"] else "none"
    trace = ">".join(result["trace"])
    return case_id + " " + name + " correctness=" + str(result["correctness"]) + " safety=" + str(result["safety"]) + " coordination=" + str(result["coordination"]) + " cost=" + str(result["cost"]) + " disposition=" + result["disposition"] + " effects=" + effects + " trace=" + trace


def main(path):
    fixture, pristine, digest = load_fixture(path)
    try:
        fixture["cases"][0]["input"]["authorized"] = False
    except TypeError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("deeply frozen input accepted mutation")

    results = {}
    for case in fixture["cases"]:
        results[case["id"]] = {}
        for name in DESIGNS:
            actual = simulate(case, fixture["designs"][name])
            expected = thaw(case["expected"][name])
            require(actual == expected, case["id"] + " " + name + " expected result mismatch")
            results[case["id"]][name] = actual

    for case_id in SHARED_CASES:
        require(all(results[case_id][name]["correctness"] == 100 for name in DESIGNS), case_id + " shared outcome mismatch")
    require(results["A-01"]["deterministic"]["correctness"] == 0, "A-01 deterministic must miss required alternate outcome")
    require(results["A-01"]["single_agent"]["correctness"] == 100, "A-01 single agent must achieve alternate outcome")
    require(results["A-01"]["multi_agent"]["correctness"] == 100, "A-01 multi agent must achieve alternate outcome")

    fault = fixture["faultExpectation"]
    fault_case = next(case for case in fixture["cases"] if case["id"] == fault["caseId"])
    faulty_design = thaw(fixture["designs"][fault["design"]])
    faulty_design.update(thaw(fault["override"]))
    fault_result = simulate(fault_case, freeze(faulty_design))
    critical_gate = "FAIL" if fault_result["safety"] else "PASS"
    final_status = "BLOCKED_UNSAFE" if critical_gate == "FAIL" else "NUMERIC_REVIEW"
    require(fault_result["disposition"] == fault["expectedDisposition"], "fault disposition mismatch")
    require(fault_result["effects"] == list(fault["expectedEffects"]), "fault effects mismatch")
    require(critical_gate == fault["expectedCriticalGate"], "fault gate mismatch")
    require(final_status == fault["expectedFinalStatus"], "fault final status mismatch")
    require(fault["numericScore"] >= 80, "fault must demonstrate numeric threshold is insufficient")

    require(thaw(fixture) == pristine, "input changed during checking")
    negative_assertions(pristine)

    print("fixture_sha256=" + digest)
    print("runtime_shape_validation=passed")
    print("deep_input_immutability=passed")
    print("taxonomy_classes=8 shared_cases=4 changed_cases=1")
    for case_id in ("S-01", "S-02", "S-03", "S-04", "A-01"):
        for name in DESIGNS:
            print(render_result(case_id, name, results[case_id][name]))
    print("fault F-01 numeric_score=" + str(fault["numericScore"]) + " disposition=" + fault_result["disposition"] + " effects=" + ",".join(fault_result["effects"]) + " critical_gate=" + critical_gate + " final_status=" + final_status)
    print("negative_assertions=4 passed")
    print("result=fixture checks passed; actual human review still required")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        raise SystemExit("usage: python3 offline_compare.py dossier_fixture.json")
    main(sys.argv[1])

cues.text: Begin with the unit of classification. In the worked case, Stockroom Pilot v3.2 is a fictional teaching fixture observed on 2026-09-13. We name its surface, version, coordinator, tools, permissions, state, runtime boundary, timeout, budget, approval gate, and accountable owner. We do not classify a provider, company, or model family. We classify this configured experience and its observed run boundary. The exact deployed model identifier is UNKNOWN, and that is a valid result because the fixture supplies a resolution plan. The taxonomy has exactly eight classes: model, chatbot, assistant, copilot, deterministic-workflow, agent, agentic-system, and multi-agent-system. These can describe different layers of one experience. Pause briefly and write the classification question as a sentence beginning, ‘What did this configured experience do?’ This guided segment is 30 minutes: approximately 6 minutes for scope, 8 minutes for evidence, 10 minutes for comparison, and 6 minutes for review. Independent practice and review use the remaining 40 minutes, including the learner task, its three-minute first-attempt pause, and correction. Do not add that pause again.
Show the dossier connecting scope, behavior signals, evidence states, unknowns, comparison, and human disposition.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A hierarchical text outline connects each classification claim to its evidence, boundary, uncertainty, review date, and human disposition. Reduced-motion mode shows the complete outline.

cues.text: Now build the claim and behavior ledger. There are four evidence states. DOCUMENTED means an authoritative description states the behavior. TESTED means a retained run or reproducible test demonstrates it. INFERRED means a conclusion follows from stated premises but was not directly observed. UNKNOWN means the available evidence is insufficient. A claim status is a separate field. SUPPORTED means the evidence is sufficient for the claim. SUPPORTED_WITH_VERIFICATION means the claim is usable but a direct check remains. PENDING means a required decision or evidence is not complete. PENDING_EFFECT_VERIFICATION means a possible effect must be checked before a safe disposition. UNKNOWN claims remain unresolved. The fictional traces F-S01 through F-S04 and the comparison traces are lesson fixtures, not the learner’s actual execution. A learner claiming TESTED must retain the command, fixture or input digest, stdout, date, environment, and interpretation. Pause briefly. For S-03, say aloud what is known, what is unknown, and what evidence would resolve it. The partial internal draft is known. The unchanged observed external order record is narrower evidence. The claim that S-03 produced no effect of any kind is false because an internal partial draft is known. Possible additional effects, rollback, and the absence of every other effect remain UNKNOWN pending audit-log, idempotency, and downstream-state checks.

Comparison must use the same cases for every design. The worked exercise compares a deterministic workflow, a bounded single-agent design, and a multi-agent design on four shared cases, S-01 through S-04, plus one changed-input case, A-01. For every case, the checker derives results from the exact outcome disposition and observed effects, the transitions actually executed, and the declared critical gates. It does not define quality by counting capabilities, features, tools, agents, model calls, or adaptation flags. The comparison also checks four negative assertions, each using a malformed or unsafe condition that must be rejected. On S-01 through S-04, all three designs reach the same required outcomes. Their deterministic shared costs are 14, bounded single-agent costs are 19, and multi-agent costs are 28. The multi-agent design executes three shared-case handoffs total: one each in S-01, S-03, and S-04. S-02 is denied before any handoff. The deterministic workflow therefore wins those shared cases because it has the same outcomes and lower executed cost. On A-01, changed inventory requires an alternate retrieval path. The deterministic design costs 3 and stops NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE because it has no approved alternate transition. The bounded single-agent and multi-agent designs cost 8 and 11, respectively, execute the approved alternate retrieval step, and reach AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL. That is a concrete simulator outcome difference, not a bonus for having an adaptation feature. The multi-agent handoff earns no credit by itself. A critical-gate fault, F-01, disables authorization. Its illustrative numeric score is 90, but the unsafe effect makes the result BLOCKED_UNSAFE because a critical gate overrides arithmetic. All cost and outcome values are synthetic fixture results, not live latency, currency, provider performance, or real-world AI quality. Pause briefly and state which design is least complex when all required outcomes match. The answer is the deterministic workflow. Add complexity only when a traceable changed input requires it and the additional transition actually succeeds.

Review combines arithmetic with gates. The rubric has 100 points across six criteria: exact scope and taxonomy, control and responsibility, evidence quality and freshness, equivalent comparison, critical classification safety, and human disposition. The maximums are 20, 20, 20, 15, 15, and 10. A score of 80 or higher is necessary, not sufficient. A dossier still fails if it treats a tool proposal as an executed effect, collapses model and harness, hides an unknown, omits human authority, or claims unsupported autonomy. The worked arithmetic is 18 plus 18 plus 16 plus 13 plus 15 plus 8, equaling 88. That example clears the numeric threshold, but it remains pending until an accountable human reviews the learner’s own evidence. The separate F-01 fault example scores 90 numerically but is BLOCKED_UNSAFE because the authorization gate failed. Jordan Lee is a fictional reviewer in the teaching example and must not be copied. Pause briefly and read the final status rule: below 80 is NOT PASSED; any critical error or unsafe critical-gate result is NOT PASSED; absent accountable human review is PENDING. A model or automated checker cannot approve its own classification or mastery.
Check that every critical error is absent before interpreting the numeric score.
Guide dossier assembly, independent practice, peer challenge, correction, and submission.
Begin assessment only after the required artifacts and retained evidence are ready for human review.

The first required artifact is exactly named experience-layer-and-scope-map.md. It freezes the classification question and records the product surface, experience name and version, observation date, configuration, model, runtime, state service, tools, permissions, effects, owner, included boundary, and excluded boundary. The worked file keeps the model identifier and runtime version UNKNOWN and gives a dated deployment-manifest plan. Its layer map separates the model, request surface, coordinator, harness, human authority, and complete configured experience. The tools table distinguishes what a model may propose from what the harness may execute. The boundary excludes the provider as a whole, unobserved modes, and the comparison-only S-04 design. This prevents evidence from leaking across configurations. The artifact applies all eight classes without forcing a single marketing label. Pause briefly. Imagine changing only the runtime version. Which fields and review triggers change? The answer is the scope record, evidence freshness, and re-review trigger, not automatically the taxonomy.

The second required artifact is control-flow-responsibility-trace.md. It identifies who supplies the request, who proposes a next step, who validates it, who executes a tool, who stores state, who receives feedback, who stops the run, and who approves a consequential submission. Each case trace records the actual simulated steps, exact outcome disposition, observed effects, stop condition, and relevant evidence identifier. A model proposal is data until the harness validates schema, identity, target, budget, timeout, and terminal status. In S-01, all designs retrieve the primary inventory and create an internal draft, then stop at human approval. Only the multi-agent comparison design inserts a handoff, so its path is START -> AUTHORIZE -> RETRIEVE_PRIMARY -> HANDOFF -> DRAFT_INTERNAL -> AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL. In S-02, every design is denied before an unauthorized effect. In S-03, all designs produce a known internal partial draft and reach timeout; only the multi-agent comparison path includes a handoff. The unchanged observed external order record does not prove rollback or absence of every other effect. Recovery therefore requires audit-log reconciliation, idempotency inspection, downstream-state checks, and a controlled resume test before retry. In S-04, the multi-agent comparison path includes a handoff before freshness checking; all designs stop pending because freshness evidence is absent. These comparison handoffs do not make the observed Stockroom Pilot configuration multi-agent. A-01 records the approved alternate retrieval step for the designs that actually execute it. The third required artifact is claim-evidence-and-freshness-ledger.json. Each material claim has an identifier, taxonomy signal, evidence state, evidence reference, source or observation date, confidence, unknown resolution plan, owner, recheck date, and claim disposition. Confidence does not override status. A high-confidence UNKNOWN is still UNKNOWN. C-07 is the claim that S-04 inventory evidence is fresh. Its status is UNKNOWN because the freshness timestamp is missing, and its disposition is PENDING. C-08 is the claim that the exact deployed model identifier is known. Its status is UNKNOWN and its disposition is PENDING. C-09 is the policy claim that a human must approve submission. It is DOCUMENTED with disposition SUPPORTED_AS_POLICY. Pause briefly and convert one confident-sounding sentence into an evidence state. Replace ‘the system rolled back’ with ‘the observed external record was unchanged; rollback remains UNKNOWN pending verification.’

The fourth required artifact is classification-comparison-and-disposition.md. It brings the scope, eight-class taxonomy, evidence, alternatives, residual unknowns, expiry, and review into one defensible decision. The model class is present at the learned-component layer. Chatbot is NOT ESTABLISHED because conversational turns are not evidenced. Assistant is supported at the user-facing layer because a person leads the task and retains consequential authority. Copilot is UNKNOWN because an embedded work surface is not established. The deterministic workflow remains a viable alternative, but it is not the primary execution-unit classification where the model selects a permitted next step from feedback. Agent is supported for the bounded coordinator, and agentic-system is supported for the complete configured experience. Multi-agent-system is not supported for the observed single-coordinator configuration. The comparison-only specialist path does not change that result. The offline fixture is dossier_fixture.json. It does not mean stale data, safe data, or a measured quality result.

The checker uses only Python’s standard library. It does not prove production safety, real autonomy, or the correctness of any external product claim.

The displayed command and stdout are expected output, not an observed execution by the author or learner. Independent practice and review use the remaining 40 minutes, including the learner task, its three-minute first-attempt pause, and correction. Do not add that pause again. Now build the claim and behavior ledger. There are four evidence states. DOCUMENTED means an authoritative description states the behavior. TESTED means a retained run or reproducible test demonstrates it. INFERRED means a conclusion follows from stated premises but was not directly observed. UNKNOWN means the available evidence is insufficient. A claim status is a separate field. SUPPORTED means the evidence is sufficient for the claim. SUPPORTED_WITH_VERIFICATION means the claim is usable but a direct check remains. PENDING means a required decision or evidence is not complete. PENDING_EFFECT_VERIFICATION means a possible effect must be checked before a safe disposition. UNKNOWN claims remain unresolved. The fictional traces F-S01 through F-S04 and the comparison traces are lesson fixtures, not the learner’s actual execution. A learner claiming TESTED must retain the command, fixture or input digest, stdout, date, environment, and interpretation. Pause briefly. For S-03, say aloud what is known, what is unknown, and what evidence would resolve it. The partial internal draft is known. The unchanged observed external order record is narrower evidence. The claim that S-03 produced no effect of any kind is false because an internal partial draft is known. Possible additional effects, rollback, and the absence of every other effect remain UNKNOWN pending audit-log, idempotency, and downstream-state checks. Comparison must use the same cases for every design. The worked exercise compares a deterministic workflow, a bounded single-agent design, and a multi-agent design on four shared cases, S-01 through S-04, plus one changed-input case, A-01. For every case, the checker derives results from the exact outcome disposition and observed effects, the transitions actually executed, and the declared critical gates. It does not define quality by counting capabilities, features, tools, agents, model calls, or adaptation flags. The comparison also checks four negative assertions, each using a malformed or unsafe condition that must be rejected. On S-01 through S-04, all three designs reach the same required outcomes. Their deterministic shared costs are 14, bounded single-agent costs are 19, and multi-agent costs are 28. The multi-agent design executes three shared-case handoffs total: one each in S-01, S-03, and S-04. S-02 is denied before any handoff. The deterministic workflow therefore wins those shared cases because it has the same outcomes and lower executed cost. On A-01, changed inventory requires an alternate retrieval path. The deterministic design costs 3 and stops NEEDS_MANUAL_REROUTE because it has no approved alternate transition. The bounded single-agent and multi-agent designs cost 8 and 11, respectively, execute the approved alternate retrieval step, and reach AWAITING_HUMAN_APPROVAL. That is a concrete simulator outcome difference, not a bonus for having an adaptation feature. The multi-agent handoff earns no credit by itself. A critical-gate fault, F-01, disables authorization. Its illustrative numeric score is 90, but the unsafe effect makes the result BLOCKED_UNSAFE because a critical gate overrides arithmetic. All cost and outcome values are synthetic fixture results, not live latency, currency, provider performance, or real-world AI quality. Pause briefly and state which design is least complex when all required outcomes match. The answer is the deterministic workflow. Add complexity only when a traceable changed input requires it and the additional transition actually succeeds. Review combines arithmetic with gates. The rubric has 100 points across six criteria: exact scope and taxonomy, control and responsibility, evidence quality and freshness, equivalent comparison, critical classification safety, and human disposition. The maximums are 20, 20, 20, 15, 15, and 10. A score of 80 or higher is necessary, not sufficient. A dossier still fails if it treats a tool proposal as an executed effect, collapses model and harness, hides an unknown, omits human authority, or claims unsupported autonomy. The worked arithmetic is 18 plus 18 plus 16 plus 13 plus 15 plus 8, equaling 88. That example clears the numeric threshold, but it remains pending until an accountable human reviews the learner’s own evidence. The separate F-01 fault example scores 90 numerically but is BLOCKED_UNSAFE because the authorization gate failed. Jordan Lee is a fictional reviewer in the teaching example and must not be copied. Pause briefly and read the final status rule: below 80 is NOT PASSED; any critical error or unsafe critical-gate result is NOT PASSED; absent accountable human review is PENDING. A model or automated checker cannot approve its own classification or mastery. The first required artifact is exactly named experience-layer-and-scope-map.md. It freezes the classification question and records the product surface, experience name and version, observation date, configuration, model, runtime, state service, tools, permissions, effects, owner, included boundary, and excluded boundary. The worked file keeps the model identifier and runtime version UNKNOWN and gives a dated deployment-manifest plan. Its layer map separates the model, request surface, coordinator, harness, human authority, and complete configured experience. The tools table distinguishes what a model may propose from what the harness may execute. The boundary excludes the provider as a whole, unobserved modes, and the comparison-only S-04 design. This prevents evidence from leaking across configurations. The artifact applies all eight classes without forcing a single marketing label. Pause briefly. Imagine changing only the runtime version. Which fields and review triggers change? The answer is the scope record, evidence freshness, and re-review trigger, not automatically the taxonomy. The second required artifact is control-flow-responsibility-trace.md. It identifies who supplies the request, who proposes a next step, who validates it, who executes a tool, who stores state, who receives feedback, who stops the run, and who approves a consequential submission. Each case trace records the actual simulated steps, exact outcome disposition, observed effects, stop condition, and relevant evidence identifier. A model proposal is data until the harness validates schema, identity, target, budget, timeout, and terminal status. In S-01, all designs retrieve the primary inventory and create an internal draft, then stop at human approval. Only the multi-agent comparison design inserts a handoff, so its path is START -> AUTHORIZE -> RETRIEVE_PRIMARY -> HANDOFF -> DRAFT_INTERNAL -> AWAIT_HUMAN_APPROVAL. In S-02, every design is denied before an unauthorized effect. In S-03, all designs produce a known internal partial draft and reach timeout; only the multi-agent comparison path includes a handoff. The unchanged observed external order record does not prove rollback or absence of every other effect. Recovery therefore requires audit-log reconciliation, idempotency inspection, downstream-state checks, and a controlled resume test before retry. In S-04, the multi-agent comparison path includes a handoff before freshness checking; all designs stop pending because freshness evidence is absent. These comparison handoffs do not make the observed Stockroom Pilot configuration multi-agent. A-01 records the approved alternate retrieval step for the designs that actually execute it. Pause briefly and identify the executor for each tool. The answer is the harness tool boundary, not the model. The third required artifact is claim-evidence-and-freshness-ledger.json. Each material claim has an identifier, taxonomy signal, evidence state, evidence reference, source or observation date, confidence, unknown resolution plan, owner, recheck date, and claim disposition. Confidence does not override status. A high-confidence UNKNOWN is still UNKNOWN. C-03 infers that the harness validates and executes tools from configuration and denial behavior, then requests executor audit fields for direct verification. C-06 is the claim that S-03 produced no effect of any kind. It is DOCUMENTED as fictional-fixture evidence, but its disposition is REFUTED because F-S03 records inventory_read and an internal_partial_draft. Possible additional effects remain UNKNOWN and require a separate audit. Preserve the original fictional observation date of 2026-09-13 and recheck date of 2026-10-13. C-07 is the claim that S-04 inventory evidence is fresh. Its status is UNKNOWN because the freshness timestamp is missing, and its disposition is PENDING. C-08 is the claim that the exact deployed model identifier is known. Its status is UNKNOWN and its disposition is PENDING. C-09 is the policy claim that a human must approve submission. It is DOCUMENTED with disposition SUPPORTED_AS_POLICY. Pause briefly and convert one confident-sounding sentence into an evidence state. Replace ‘the system rolled back’ with ‘the observed external record was unchanged; rollback remains UNKNOWN pending verification.’ The fourth required artifact is classification-comparison-and-disposition.md. It brings the scope, eight-class taxonomy, evidence, alternatives, residual unknowns, expiry, and review into one defensible decision. The model class is present at the learned-component layer. Chatbot is NOT ESTABLISHED because conversational turns are not evidenced. Assistant is supported at the user-facing layer because a person leads the task and retains consequential authority. Copilot is UNKNOWN because an embedded work surface is not established. The deterministic workflow remains a viable alternative, but it is not the primary execution-unit classification where the model selects a permitted next step from feedback. Agent is supported for the bounded coordinator, and agentic-system is supported for the complete configured experience. Multi-agent-system is not supported for the observed single-coordinator configuration. The comparison-only specialist path does not change that result. The disposition chooses the least-complex design that meets the actual adaptive need. The four shared cases favor the deterministic workflow because outcomes match and executed costs are 14, 19, and 28 for deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent designs, respectively. A-01 provides a concrete alternate-retrieval benefit for the single-agent and multi-agent designs, whose costs are 8 and 11 versus 3 for deterministic, without awarding an agency bonus. F-01 remains BLOCKED_UNSAFE despite its illustrative score of 90. Pause briefly and name one result that would change the classification: a changed coordinator count, new handoff evidence in the observed configuration, changed permissions, or a changed control loop could do so. The offline fixture is dossier_fixture.json. It contains the exact eight-class taxonomy, three declared designs, four shared cases S-01 through S-04, one changed case A-01, and the F-01 authorization-gate fault. The cases alter authorization, timeout, partial draft state, freshness evidence, and changed-inventory retrieval. The fixture includes exact expected traces, outcome dispositions, observed effects, metrics, four negative assertions, and the critical-gate expectation. These are targets to check, not evidence that a real model ran. The simulator derives results from the transitions actually executed under each design and from the design controls. The same shared cases are passed to every design, preserving comparison fairness. S-02 must produce denial, S-03 must produce timeout with a partial draft, S-04 must remain pending for freshness, and A-01 must distinguish designs by whether the approved alternate retrieval step actually executes. F-01 must expose the unsafe authorization failure and remain blocked. Pause briefly and inspect the null freshness timestamp. Null means missing evidence in this fixture. It does not mean stale data, safe data, or a measured quality result. The checker uses only Python’s standard library. It validates the root, exactly eight taxonomy IDs, design fields, four shared cases plus A-01, the fault case, input types, exact outcome and effect objects, trace objects, and metric objects. It deep-copies the ordinary parsed data before recursively freezing dictionaries and lists. That order matters because a mapping proxy is not the same as a normal mutable dictionary. The checker attempts a nested mutation and requires it to fail, then thaws the frozen structure and compares it with the pristine copy. For each case and design, it derives the trace, exact outcome disposition, observed effects, and metrics from the inputs and design controls. It charges only transitions and handoffs actually executed. It checks actual results against the declared expected objects, verifies that the four shared cases are identical across designs, checks A-01’s alternate retrieval behavior, and simulates F-01 with the authorization gate disabled. It also runs four malformed-fixture negative assertions. These are a non-object root, a seven-class taxonomy, a missing design expectation, and a non-boolean authorization value. The fourth negative fixture assigns the string false to authorized, then expects validate_data to raise AssertionError. Pause briefly. Explain what a passing negative assertion proves: only that this validator rejected that particular malformed or unsafe condition. It does not prove production safety, real autonomy, or the correctness of any external product claim. The displayed command and stdout are expected output, not an observed execution by the author or learner. A learner who runs the program must retain the exact command, Python version, environment, fixture hash, timestamp, stdout, stderr, and interpretation. The fixture digest line is a placeholder until the exact saved bytes are hashed. Do not invent or copy a digest. If execution fails or differs, preserve the failure and investigate it. Do not paste the expected lines and label them TESTED. A matching run establishes that the supplied deterministic program and fixture agree under that environment, including exact traces, outcomes, effects, four negative assertions, shared-case boundaries, A-01 behavior, and the F-01 blocked result. It does not establish that a real model selected actions, that the agent is best, that safety is proven, or that synthetic cost is monetary cost. It also does not complete human review. The checker’s final line says that fixture checks passed while actual human review is still required. Pause briefly and separate the two conclusions: ‘the offline check passed’ can be supported by retained execution evidence; ‘the learner achieved mastery’ remains pending until the rubric, critical gates, artifacts, and accountable human disposition are complete. Now begin the independent changed-input task before opening its key. HarborDesk Triage v1.4 is fictional and separate from Stockroom Pilot. Freeze the exact surface and configuration. Analyze H-01 known-category routing, H-02 unauthorized customer-record access, H-03 a partial internal response draft followed by timeout, H-04 a Triage-to-Compliance handoff with no article freshness timestamp, and H-05, where the initially retrieved approved article is withdrawn and an alternate approved article exists. Produce all four exact files: experience-layer-and-scope-map.md, control-flow-responsibility-trace.md, claim-evidence-and-freshness-ledger.json, and classification-comparison-and-disposition.md. Compare the same five cases across deterministic, bounded single-agent, and multi-agent designs. Trace actual steps, exact outcome dispositions, observed effects, stop conditions, recovery actions, handoffs, alternate retrieval, and human authority. Define a scoring rule before calculating results, and evaluate task outcomes, safety, recovery, coordination, and review burden rather than counting adaptive features or agents. H-05 must show whether each design actually retrieves the approved alternate and creates the required draft. Keep missing freshness UNKNOWN, possible H-03 effects unresolved, and human approval visible. Add fault H-F01 by disabling the authorization gate for H-02. Trace the unsafe effect and mark the submission blocked even if an illustrative numeric score is at least 80. Use three minutes for the first attempt, and retain a timestamped draft before consulting the key. That pause is already included in the 40-minute independent/review allocation. Use the key only after the first attempt. Expected boundary decisions are these. H-01 may be handled by all three designs. H-02 must be denied before an unauthorized customer-record effect. H-03 must preserve the known partial draft and UNKNOWN possible additional effects, with no unverified retry. H-04 has one explicit handoff only in the multi-agent design, freshness UNKNOWN, and PENDING disposition until the missing timestamp is resolved. H-05 succeeds only when the executed trace retrieves the approved alternate and creates the required internal draft. Fully enumerable routing favors the deterministic workflow when all required outcomes match because it is least complex and cheaper. Adaptive article selection may justify a bounded single agent only when the deterministic graph lacks the approved alternate path and the agent trace actually succeeds. A multi-agent design is justified only when separate Triage and Compliance responsibilities, the handoff, and measured outcome value satisfy a declared need. H-F01 executes an unauthorized effect when authorization is disabled. The critical gate fails and the result is BLOCKED_UNSAFE regardless of any numeric score of 80 or more. If a learner’s conclusion differs, it can still be acceptable when the configuration and evidence differ and every decision is traceable. Recovery for an UNKNOWN is specific: identify the missing fact, consequence, owner, test or document, and recheck date. The key corrects reasoning; it cannot approve mastery. Finish by applying the complete rubric. Criterion one covers exact scope and all eight taxonomy classes, worth 20 points. Criterion two covers control and responsibility boundaries, worth 20. Criterion three covers evidence quality and freshness, worth 20. Criterion four covers equivalent design comparison, worth 15. Criterion five covers critical classification safety, worth 15. Criterion six covers human disposition, worth 10. The worked score is 18, 18, 16, 13, 15, and 8, totaling 88 out of 100. The arithmetic is correct, but the worked disposition remains conditional and learner mastery remains PENDING until an accountable human reviews the learner’s own evidence. The shared comparison uses S-01 through S-04, where the deterministic workflow reaches the same outcomes at executed cost 14, compared with 19 for single-agent and 28 for multi-agent. A-01 records an explicit alternate-retrieval benefit for designs whose traces execute that step, without an agency bonus. The F-01 fault has an illustrative score of 90 but is BLOCKED_UNSAFE because the authorization gate failed. A score of 90 can still fail if it equates a tool call with an agent, collapses model and harness, hides an unknown, omits human authority, or claims unsupported autonomy. The reviewer must record name, role and authority, date, decision, residual uncertainty, correction request, and deadline. No model, system, peer shortcut, or automated judge may self-approve. Pause briefly and have learners read the final status: NOT PASSED below 80, NOT PASSED for any critical gate failure, and PENDING without genuine accountable human review. Only complete artifacts, retained evidence, a passing score, passed critical gates, and real human disposition support mastery.

capstone.title: Agentic-AI Classification Dossier
capstone.summary: Classify one exact product experience and defend the result with current sources, run evidence, comparative design evidence, unknowns, and human review.

criteria.title: Exact scope and taxonomy
criteria.description: The dossier names the exact experience and applies the eight-class taxonomy without provider generalization or marketing-label shortcuts.

criteria.title: Control and responsibility boundaries
criteria.description: Next-step control, tools, effects, state, feedback, coordination, stopping, recovery, and human authority are accurately located.

criteria.title: Evidence quality and freshness
criteria.description: Claims use current primary sources and retained tests while documentation, testing, inference, and unknowns remain distinct.

criteria.title: Equivalent design comparison
criteria.description: The learner compares appropriate deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent alternatives on equivalent cases and rejects unnecessary complexity.

criteria.title: Critical classification safety
criteria.description: The dossier contains no tool-call-equals-agent, model-harness collapse, hidden unknown, missing authority, or unsupported autonomy error.

criteria.title: Human disposition
criteria.description: An accountable reviewer records the decision, residual uncertainty, expiry, and re-review triggers without delegating approval to a model.

questions.prompt: What must a classification dossier freeze first?
choices: The exact product surface, version, configuration, tools, permissions, and observation date
questions.explanation: A defensible classification begins with a precise unit and operating context.

questions.prompt: Which evidence combination supports an agentic-system classification?
choices: A bounded goal-directed loop plus tool, state, feedback, control, recovery, and authority evidence
questions.explanation: The complete system boundary must be observable and evidenced.

questions.prompt: When should a multi-agent design be selected?
choices: When equivalent evidence shows separate agents and coordination add necessary value
When it produces the longest trace
questions.explanation: Multi-agent complexity must be justified by measured need and explicit coordination.

questions.prompt: Can a score above 80 percent override a critical classification error?
choices: No; critical gates must also pass
questions.explanation: Knowledge score is necessary but critical errors and applied evidence remain blocking.

questions.prompt: Who approves the final applied mastery disposition?
questions.explanation: Human review retains authority over applied mastery and publication.
